key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines weld-pool simulation, AI surrogates, and robot simulation to screen in-space welding conditions and control strategies before physical testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support adaptive robotic welding for on-orbit assembly and repair while reducing reliance on scarce flight-like tests.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates approximate weld-model outputs.
A simulated UR5 uses proportional control to adjust power-source settings as travel speed falls near a seam corner.
evidence_signal: The GP achieved lower cross-validated error across all eight outputs, covered 74/80 held-out solver responses with nominal 90% predictive intervals, and enabled simulated control yielding 12/12 operating points within an illustrative width band versus 9/12 open-loop.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation remain necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
